attribution.note: Marcus makes and endorses the assessment himself.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the model, negative assessment, and limitation to progress by the post date.

contract.note: Reading the informal assessment as failure to meet performance and release expectations is ordinary in context. Literal inability to run would be an unjustified reading.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous reporting links the delay to insufficient capability improvements. Fortune relays the WSJ rather than independently confirming it.
Reports executive dissatisfaction with Behemoth's progress during the target period. It shares the WSJ source with e1.
Meta's company disclosure reports benchmark strengths and teacher-model use. These qualify a literal failure claim but do not establish that Behemoth met release expectations.
The July account concerns developments outside the target period and cannot establish the model's status by May 17 under this contract.

reviews.rationale: Contemporaneous reports attribute Behemoth's delay to inadequate performance improvements and stalled progress, satisfying the fair plain reading. Meta's claimed benchmark successes do not negate those shortcomings. The supporting reports share one underlying source and rely on unnamed informants.

attribution.note: The profitability assertion is Marcus's own parenthetical statement, not a claim attributed to Altman.

semantics.note: The normalization faithfully extracts the historical profitability claim about OpenAI, assessed as of the post date.

contract.note: Annual company-level net profitability is an ordinary reading. Credible financial reporting is a reasonable evidentiary standard for this private company.

evidence.note: Salon directly reports that OpenAI had not turned a profit. Its accompanying 2024 figure remains a projection, not a finalized annual result.
This reports a projected 2024 loss. The packet labels it realized, but an expectation does not establish realized annual net income.
Reports losses in 2022 and, through the year-over-year comparison, 2021. It supports those years without independently covering the entire history.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's credible-reporting standard, Salon's direct account of no prior profit and reported historical losses support the claim. No profitable reporting period appears in the packet. Support is qualified by missing annual accounts and unaudited reporting; the 2024 projection is not treated as a realized result.
